strings.en:
Mai finally made good on all her talk. She brought me something I've never seen before, developed far beyond the borders of Cantha. It isn't clear how she got her hands on it, but I'm not going to press her on that.

The device in question is a turret once fastened to an airship. It is powered by heating water, which powers a turbine to produce a current. All of that involves a massive casing. It's amazing the airship could fly at all.

Mai took it strangely personally when I said the tech was unsophisticated. I've seen her work with much more complex systems, surely she is capable of recognizing mediocrity. I've asked if she thinks she can get her hands on more of it, and while she won't commit, she is optimistic.

Renyak,  
  
I hope you are well, but unfortunately I'm writing with a knife to my throat.  
  
Sentius informed us that some adversary named "B" is having us march on Cragstead; a small village just outside of Hoelbrak. I haven't met such a character myself, but Sentius and Falx are...shaken by B's sway. They're already facing enough pushback from the dredge for treating their women with "disrespect," so we're taking a slightly more diplomatic route. I will be leading the charge while they remain in the war room.  
  
When the place is burned to a crisp, I will deliver the supplies you called for. I must say, whatever experiment they have you working on that requires that much Deldrimor steel... Well, it's going to take multiple trips to deliver it all. It better be worth the trip.  
  
Go with the might of a rock, the will of steel.  
  
Your brother, Caros

Track[pl:"Copies of Track"] 5: Taimi's Game Part 1

Another exploration team returned earlier. I've pored over their findings, and one thing that's becoming increasingly clear is that this just couldn't have been a major population center. There are no homes, few living areas at all, and none of the infrastructure needed for a town, much less a city.  
  
I'll concede that some of these structures are massive, and obviously this place served some very important purpose. But this is not the lost capital city of the seers that others seem to think it is. Determining why they chose Castora and what they built here will be an important focal point going forward, but we need to be careful to see only what is actually there.  
  
Some of my more optimistic colleagues think that the capital city must be further inland, and I can understand why. This civilization was once the mightiest in Tyria, so surely we must have simply not yet found the ruins they left behind.  
  
But I offer instead a sobering theory: we will never find it, because it's gone. The mursaat cast down every stone they found, and the only reason the ruins remain here is because they never found this island. We should treasure everything we uncover here, because it's likely to be the last we ever find.
